---
title: 'Day 4: Functional-group inspection workbench'
---

A **5–10 minute exploration**, using a prediction before each control change. The diagram and result update locally; no network service is used.

## Predict first

In lactic acid, should selecting “alcohol” highlight every O atom? Predict which O belongs to the alcohol and which atoms belong to the carboxylic acid.

## Explore

1. Inspect lactic acid with the highlight hidden. Locate its two oxygen-containing motifs, then reveal alcohol and acid separately.

2. Select ethanoic acid and ask for alcohol. Explain the absence of an alcohol match even though an O–H bond exists.

3. Compare ether with ketone, then inspect the neutral drawn glycine form for an amine and acid. Change the selected group before revealing so each attempt starts with your own prediction.

## Take-away

Choose two molecules with oxygen and explain why one local O–H or C–O bond does not classify all their functional groups.

## Model and limits

The workbench recognises the complete motifs supplied in these particular structures; it is not an automatic general chemical classifier. Highlighted atoms identify the chosen local site. Neutral drawn glycine is used to inspect connectivity; actual aqueous protonation depends on pH.
